newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles mayor welcomes changes to $4 bln plan.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles mayor welcomes changes to $4 bln plan.

text.p: Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan's budget director on Tuesday welcomed several changes to the city's $4 billion spending plan for fiscal 1997-1998, but said he would not support a boost in city council funding.

The amendments, approved by the City Council on Monday, included $1 million to expand park staffing, $1.2 million of additional library funding, and $500,000 to set up new business improvement districts.
Council members also approved a $1.5 million boost in funding for City Council offices.
"Overall, we're very pleased," said Chris O'Donnell, Riordan's budget director. "The changes that they (the City Council) made to the budget overall were very minor."
But O'Donnell said he was "disturbed" by the council's decision to boost funding for Council offices.
Riordan has 10 days to veto any of the amendments before returning the spending plan to the Council for final action.
The mayor's $4 billion spending plan -- $50 million smaller than last year's budget -- contained a reserve of $30 million, and seeks no new taxes.

The mayor's bond proposals -- a $465 million bond for police and fire facilities and a $151 million bond for library improvements -- were not included in the budget pact. They will be reviewed by the City Council separately.
